## AbilityBase

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/AbilityBase.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

One thing a pawn can do, such as walk, jump, swing or dash: a child of the pawn's [`AbilityManager`](#abilitymanager).

Its settings come from its `definition`, a Resource every pawn using it shares (ability spec 3): the node holds that reference and its state, and reads each setting from the definition. Empty, it runs with its kind's defaults.
Extend it, override `make_default_definition()` for a kind with settings of its own, and override `can_start()`, `start()`, `tick()`, `stop()` and, for counters that run all the time, `every_tick()` (with `can_sleep()`). A quick ability can instead set base settings in `_init()`: they go into a definition of its own. LOCOMOTION abilities move the pawn every tick they're chosen (one runs at a time); ACTION abilities start on a press of their `trigger_action`, at once or for a `duration`. Players' keys and AI behaviours press the same actions. Times are set in seconds and kept in ticks (60 a second).
Rollback: whatever an ability keeps between ticks must be named in `get_pushed_properties()` (its setter calls `push_state()`) or `get_rollback_properties()` (read at every commit); the base already covers its own timers and step state. It can also be built from [`AbilityStep`](#abilitystep) children (a windup, a turn, a swing) and carry [`HitInterceptor`](#hitinterceptor) children that stop hits while it runs. Design: pawn spec 8, 8.20, 8.23.

### Settings and properties

- `kind: int` = `1`: What the code does with it: move the pawn every tick, or start on a press. Set by the kind's script.
- `definition: AbilityDefinition`: The settings it runs with (ability spec 3): a file shared by every pawn that uses it, or one embedded in this node while prototyping. Empty: its kind's defaults. One of another kind falls back to the defaults, with a warning.
- `settings: AbilityDefinition` = `null`: The settings it runs with: `definition` worked out (`AbilityDefinition.resolved()`), or its kind's defaults. Read-only while playing. Set by `prepare_settings()`.
- `definition_fell_back: bool` = `false`: True if its definition was of another kind, so it runs with its kind's defaults (diagnostics lists these).
- `trigger_action: StringName`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.trigger_action`.
- `category: StringName`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.category`.
- `extra_categories: StringName[]`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.extra_categories`.
- `priority: int`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.priority`.
- `combo_positions: int[]`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.combo_positions`.
- `priority_jitter: float`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.priority_jitter`.
- `duration: float`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.duration`.
- `cooldown: float`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.cooldown`.
- `locks_out: StringName[]`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.locks_out`.
- `buffer_window: float`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.buffer_window`.
- `interrupt_priority: int`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.interrupt_priority`.
- `interrupt_threshold: int`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.interrupt_threshold`.
- `cancelled_by: StringName[]`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.cancelled_by`.
- `pauses_locomotion: bool`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.pauses_locomotion`.
- `needs_full_movement: bool`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.needs_full_movement`.
- `step_timeline: TimelineEntry[]`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.step_timeline`.
- `max_steps_ticks: int`: From the definition: `AbilityDefinition.max_steps_ticks`.
- `started_at: int` = `-1`: The tick the current (or last) timed run started.
- `ends_at: int` = `-1`: The tick the current timed run ends: the manager finishes it on its first run at or after this tick. -1: not running.
- `ready_at: int` = `0`: The tick it can start again: ready from this tick on.
- `buffer_until: int` = `0`: A press waiting in the buffer waits until this tick (not including it).
- `manager: AbilityManager` = `null`: Set by the AbilityManager.
- `jitter_salt: int` = `0`: Set by the AbilityManager: a number from its name, for the priority_jitter offset.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`
- `category_mask: int` = `0`: Its category and extra_categories as bits, with their parents'. Worked out once by the manager.
- `locks_out_mask: int` = `0`: locks_out as bits. Worked out once by the manager.
- `cancelled_by_mask: int` = `0`: cancelled_by as bits. Worked out once by the manager, so the check while playing is one bit test.
- `trigger_bit: int` = `0`: trigger_action's input bit ([`InputActions`](../controllers/REFERENCE.md#inputactions)), or 0 with none. Worked out once by the manager (pawn spec 15.2).
- `on_start_effects: Effect[]` = `[]`: From its EffectApplier children, collected once by the manager (pawn spec 8.11): on its own pawn when it starts; on a pawn it hits; on its own pawn when it hits. A [`MeleeSweepStep`](#meleesweepstep) hands the last two to the [`HitInfo`](#hitinfo).
- `on_hit_effects: Effect[]` = `[]`
- `on_hit_self_effects: Effect[]` = `[]`
- `interceptors: HitInterceptor[]` = `[]`: Its [`HitInterceptor`](#hitinterceptor)s, under it or its steps, found by the manager (pawn spec 8.23).
- `steps: AbilityStep[]` = `[]`: Its [`AbilityStep`](#abilitystep) children in tree order, found by `collect_steps()`. Empty: no steps.
- `timeline: TimelineEntry[]` = `[]`: The step timeline it runs (ability spec 6.2): its definition's `AbilityDefinition.step_timeline`, else its kind's default (`default_timeline()`), else its steps one after another in tree order; plus a manual entry for each step none names. Worked out by `collect_steps()`.
- `timeline_state: PackedInt32Array` = `PackedInt32Array()`: Its timeline's state, four numbers per entry: the tick it started, the tick it ended (-1: not yet), why it ended (`TimelineEntry.Reason`, 0 none) and where its step's count starts (the start, moved on by ticks that didn't count). Rolled back as one value. A step that only waits out its length changes nothing while it runs.
- `pawns_hit_this_run: int[]` = `[]`: The pawns its steps have hit this run (instance ids), so each is hit once across all its sweeps. Server only, never in a replay; cleared when it starts.

### Constants

- `Kind.LOCOMOTION = 0`
- `Kind.ACTION = 1`
- `NEVER = 4611686018427387904`: `ends_at` for a run with no end of its own yet (Death, while Health is 0).
- `MAX_STEP_STARTS_PER_TICK = 32`: The most steps one ability may start in one tick, a guard against steps that start and stop each other in a loop. Past it, starts are refused, the ability ends and it warns once.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: The definition a new node of this kind runs with: a new definition of the kind's class, with its defaults. Each kind overrides it.
- `kind_defaults() -> AbilityDefinition`: This kind's defaults, shared by every node of the kind.
- `prepare_settings() -> AbilityDefinition`: Works out `settings` from `definition`: its kind's defaults with none, or with one of another kind (warning). Settings written on the node (a script's _init(), old scene values, `make_definition_unique()`) go into a variant of its own on top. The manager calls it as it collects its abilities; reading a setting before then calls it too. Returns the settings.
- `use_definition(new_definition: AbilityDefinition) -> void`: Gives it another definition while playing (a weapon swap), and has the manager work out its masks and lists again. What rolls back was decided when the pawn started, so a definition that turns on a timer this ability didn't have won't roll it back.
- `make_definition_unique() -> AbilityDefinition`: Gives it settings of its own, on top of its definition, which this node alone uses: Godot's "Make Unique", while playing. Its settings can be written after that. For prototyping and tests; a shipped game uses another definition.
- `has_own_settings() -> bool`: True if it has settings of its own on top of its definition (`make_definition_unique()`, its script's _init(), or values a scene sets on the node), not only the shared ones.
- `definition_note() -> String`: What to check about where its settings come from, for diagnostics: "fell back" (a definition of another kind), "embedded" (saved in a scene, a prototype tweak), "own settings" (written on the node), or "" when it runs with a definition file or its kind's defaults.
- `get_pushed_properties() -> String[]`: The properties on this node that roll back and whose setters call `push_state()`, so the state store records them only when they change (state store spec 6.3). An ability that keeps more adds to it with `super()`. The cheap way, and the one the built-in abilities use.
- `get_rollback_properties() -> String[]`: Other properties on this node that roll back, read from the node at every commit: no setter needed, so the easy way for a quick ability, but each costs a read per pawn per tick. None in the base.
- `keeps_state(property: String) -> bool`: True if this property rolls back, either way.
- `push_state(property: StringName, value: Variant) -> void`: Records a pushed property's new value in the state store, from the next commit on (state store spec 6.3). Each property in `get_pushed_properties()` calls it from its setter, after setting the value. Nothing until the manager has registered them.
- `duration_ticks() -> int`: How many ticks a timed run lasts: duration in ticks, or max_steps_ticks when stepped. Dash and Knockback override it.
- `is_timed() -> bool`: True if it runs for a while once started (a duration, steps, or a length of its own: Dash, Death, Knockback), so it keeps `started_at` and `ends_at`. False for one that happens at once, such as Jump.
- `is_running_timed() -> bool`: True while a timed run is going.
- `is_run_over() -> bool`: True once the current run is over: the manager finishes it on this pawn's run. Set by `end_run()`, or by reaching ends_at.
- `end_run() -> void`: Ends the current run this tick: the manager finishes it (stopping its steps, starting its cooldown) before this run of the pawn is over. For steps that are done, and for an ability that decides its own end.
- `delay_run(ticks: int) -> void`: Moves the current run's deadlines this many ticks later, as if it hadn't run for them: the manager calls it while an action pauses locomotion (a Dash), so a timed locomotion's time waits. An ability with deadlines of its own moves them too, with `super()`.
- `ticks_running() -> int`: Ticks since the current run started, through this tick; 0 when not running. Worked out from `started_at`, so it rolls back.
- `ticks_before_this_run() -> int`: For `tick()`: the ticks of the run that came before this run of the pawn (0 on its first tick). This run covers `ticks_elapsed()` more.
- `ticks_left() -> int`: Ticks left of the current run, from `ends_at`; 0 when not running. For readouts.
- `cooldown_ticks_left() -> int`: Ticks until it can start again, from `ready_at`; 0 when ready. For readouts.
- `buffer_ticks_left() -> int`: Ticks a waiting press has left in its buffer, from `buffer_until`; 0 with none. For readouts.
- `is_buffered() -> bool`: True while a press waits in its buffer.
- `_running_changed(_running: bool) -> void`: Called when a timed run starts or ends, also when a rollback loads new values. [`DeathAbility`](#deathability) uses it to keep `Pawn.dead` current.
- `ticks_elapsed() -> int`: The ticks this run covers: 1, or more for a pawn running every Nth tick (pawn spec 8.21). Timers and step counts advance by it.
- `is_stepped() -> bool`: True if it's built from steps.
- `default_timeline() -> TimelineEntry[]`: The timeline it runs when its definition has none: none by default, so its steps run one after another. A kind that makes its own steps (MeleeAttack, RangedAttack) returns the timeline for them.
- `start_step(step: AbilityStep) -> void`: Starts a step from code, as a bespoke script does (ability spec 6.4): its first entry not running, started again if it already ran. Steps not in the timeline have a manual entry for this.
- `stop_step(step: AbilityStep, reason: String = "cancelled") -> void`: Stops a running step, passing the reason ("done", "released", "failed", "cancelled") to its `AbilityStep.exit()`.
- `is_step_running(step: AbilityStep) -> bool`: True while this step of this ability runs.
- `running_entry_of(step: AbilityStep) -> int`: The timeline entry this step runs in now, or -1.
- `step_ticks_of(step: AbilityStep) -> int`: Ticks a running step has counted: since it started, less the ticks that didn't count (`AbilityStep.counts_this_tick()`). Inside its own `AbilityStep.tick()`, the ticks before this one. 0 when not running.
- `start_entry(e: int) -> void`: Starts this timeline entry now: its values onto its step, then the step's enter(). Rules call it; code can too.
- `stop_entry(e: int, reason: String = "cancelled") -> void`: Stops this running timeline entry with this reason ("done", "released", "failed" or "cancelled").
- `get_running_step_names() -> PackedStringArray`: The names of the steps running now, in tree order. For readouts and debug tools.
- `current_interrupt_threshold() -> int`: Its interrupt_threshold now, before effects add: the strictest of its running steps' own, or its own when none has one.
- `make_default_interceptors() -> void`: Called by the manager when the ability has no [`HitInterceptor`](#hitinterceptor), so it can make its defaults (Dash, Parry). Nothing by default.
- `collect_steps() -> void`: Called once by the manager: finds the [`AbilityStep`](#abilitystep) children and works out its `timeline`.
- `begin_steps() -> void`: Called by the manager when the ability starts: clears the timeline's state and starts the entries due at its start.
- `run_steps(dt: float) -> void`: Called by the manager every tick the ability runs, after `tick()`: ticks each running step (in timeline order), then starts the entries whose rules now hold. A step done or released starts what follows it; one that fails ends them all. The ability ends when no step that keeps it running runs and no entry is due.
- `end_steps(reason: String = "cancelled") -> void`: Stops every running step with this reason, and puts back the step values its entries changed. The manager calls it when the ability finishes or is cancelled.
- `timeline_loaded() -> void`: After a rollback loads its state: the running entries' values go back onto their steps.
- `steps_after(step: AbilityStep) -> AbilityStep[]`: The steps whose entries start when an entry of this step ends: what comes after it, for visuals (a windup's sweep).
- `step_before(step: AbilityStep) -> AbilityStep`: The step whose end starts this step's first entry, or null: what came before it, for visuals (a recovery's sweep).
- `weapon_point(facing: float) -> Variant`: Where its weapon is now, from the first running step that says, as an offset from the pawn's feet for this facing in radians; null if none. For visuals and animation.
- `move_input() -> Vector3`: The direction the pawn is told to go, in world space, up to length 1.
- `look_yaw() -> float`: Where the pawn is told to look, around the vertical, in radians.
- `attack_reach() -> float`: How far away a target may be for the AI to use this as an attack, in metres; 0 means it isn't an attack. The AI's Attack behaviour reads it, so any attack (melee, ranged, a game's own) can be driven by one behaviour.
- `view_ticks_behind() -> float`: How many ticks behind its own the controller drew other pawns, for lag compensation.
- `held_actions() -> int`: The held actions this tick, as InputActions bits.
- `previous_held_actions() -> int`: The held actions last tick, as InputActions bits, so a press can be told from a hold.
- `read_stat(stat_name: StringName, fallback: float) -> float`: A stat from the pawn's StatManager, or fallback if there's no such stat or no StatManager.
- `can_start() -> bool`: Extra conditions for starting, such as being on the ground. Cooldowns, lockouts and combos are already checked.
- `start() -> void`: Once, when it starts.
- `tick(_dt: float) -> void`: Every tick it runs.
- `stop() -> void`: Once, when it stops, finished or cancelled.
- `every_tick(_dt: float) -> void`: Every tick, running or not. Only called on abilities whose script overrides it.
- `can_sleep() -> bool`: True if it's fine with the pawn sleeping (pawn spec 15.3). Only an ability that overrides `every_tick()` needs to answer: false while it would still change something. Jump answers false until its time off the ground is back to 0.
- `can_sleep_while_running() -> bool`: True if the pawn may sleep while it runs (pawn spec 15.3); its timer and tick wait with the pawn. Death answers true while Health is 0. Asked every tick the pawn could otherwise sleep, so keep it cheap.

## AbilityManager

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/AbilityManager.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Starts, runs and stops a pawn's abilities, and takes the hits that land on it.

A part on the pawn, added by PawnInitializer, with the abilities as its children. The pawn calls `tick_abilities()` once a tick, after its input arrives and before `move_and_slide`: one locomotion ability runs, then pressed actions start the ready ability with the highest priority. Timers are tick deadlines (ability spec 4), so nothing counts down. It owns the cancelling rules, the combo counter and the hit path. Everything that persists between ticks lives on the abilities (and the combo counter here) and rolls back. Outside code only talks to the manager:

```gdscript
pawn.ability_manager.can_start(&"jump")      # could a press start something now? (the AI asks)
pawn.ability_manager.action_for_tag(tag)     # the action to press for a kind of ability, such as movement.advanced
pawn.ability_manager.start_ability(ability)  # starts one with no trigger action, such as Knockback, by the same rules
pawn.ability_manager.receive_hit(hit)        # something hit this pawn (server)
```

Design: pawn spec 8, 8.6, 8.11, 8.16, 8.20, 8.23, 15.2.

### Settings and properties

- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`
- `combo_position: int` = `0`: The combo position the last combo ability took; 0: none yet. Pushed to the state store when it changes.
- `combo_open_until: int` = `0`: The combo window is open until this tick (not including it): a follow-up for the next position can start. Pushed when it changes.
- `readiness_version: int` = `0`: Goes up by one whenever something changes that can change what `can_start()` answers (an ability or step starting or ending, a cooldown or the combo window running out, effects changing). The AI keeps its last answer until this moves ([`AIInputs`](../ai/REFERENCE.md#aiinputs); scaling spec 6.2). Never goes down. A deadline passing moves it on when it's next read, so the AI in the input step sees a cooldown end on its tick, as `can_start()` does, before this pawn's abilities run.

### Signals

- `hit_intercepted(hit: HitInfo, interceptor: HitInterceptor)`: A [`HitInterceptor`](#hitinterceptor) stopped a hit, on the server, after its response went out (pawn spec 8.23).
- `ability_started(ability: AbilityBase)`: An ability started.
- `ability_finished(ability: AbilityBase)`: An ability stopped, finished or cancelled.
- `ability_cancelled(ability: AbilityBase, by: AbilityBase)`: An ability was cancelled by another starting, sent after `ability_finished` for it.
- `step_started(ability: AbilityBase, step: AbilityStep)`: A step of a stepped ability started (pawn spec 8.20). Sent by `AbilityBase.start_step()`.
- `step_finished(ability: AbilityBase, step: AbilityStep, reason: String)`: A step stopped; reason is "done", "released", "failed" or "cancelled". Sent by `AbilityBase.stop_step()`.
- `hit_arrived(hit: HitInfo)`: A hit reached this pawn, on the server (not dead or invulnerable). Sent before an interceptor can turn it away and before its effects land, so the AI notes every attack.
- `hit_received(hit: HitInfo)`: A hit landed, on the server, after its effects were applied (pawn spec 8.11); hit.damage_dealt is the Health it took. Not sent for a hit an interceptor stopped.
- `died(pawn: Pawn, hit: HitInfo)`: This pawn died, once, on the server, after its Death ability started. hit is what did it, or null. Parts clean up by listening.

### Functions

- `tick_abilities(dt: float) -> void`: The pawn calls this once a tick; dt is the fixed tick length. Order: deadlines passed, locomotion, then actions (see the README).
- `timers_changed() -> void`: The abilities' timers call this when one is set (pawn spec 15.2).
- `state_loaded() -> void`: After a rollback loads this pawn's state: what's worked out from the deadlines is worked out again. A loaded deadline equal to the one it replaces calls no setter, but the soonest one still ahead depends on the tick, which went back.
- `readiness_changed() -> void`: Moves `readiness_version` on for a change made outside the abilities; the EffectManager calls it when effects change.
- `ready_follows_body(action: StringName) -> bool`: True if an ability on this action has its own `AbilityBase.can_start()`, which can change without telling the manager (Jump needs the ground). The AI asks such an action at every decision, whatever `readiness_version` says.
- `can_sleep() -> bool`: True if the pawn can sleep as far as its abilities go (pawn spec 15.3): no timer running (unless that ability can wait), no combo window open, and every every_tick() ability agrees.
- `can_start(action: StringName) -> bool`: True if pressing this action now would start something, counting abilities it would cancel. Changes nothing; looks only at the abilities on that action.
- `action_for_tag(tag: StringName) -> StringName`: The action to press to start an ability in this group (a category or extra_category such as &"movement.advanced"): the highest-priority one that could start now, boosts included; &"" if none. For the AI, so a behaviour asks for a kind of ability, not one by name. It answers with an action because everything a pawn does goes through its (rolled back) input. Changes nothing.
- `start_ability(ability: AbilityBase) -> bool`: Starts an ability by the same rules as a press (cooldown, can_start, cancelling what conflicts). For abilities started by code, such as Knockback. One already running starts again from the beginning. Returns false if it couldn't start.
- `intercept_hit(hit: HitInfo) -> HitInterceptor`: The first active TURN_AWAY interceptor that stops this hit, or null (pawn spec 8.23). Its response and `hit_intercepted` have gone out. A reply to an interception isn't turned away.
- `is_invulnerable() -> bool`: True while a MISS-stage interceptor is on, such as a Dash's first 0.18 s. Hits don't arrive and harmful effects are refused.
- `is_busy() -> bool`: True while a timed action is running, such as an attack's swing.
- `has_action(action: StringName) -> bool`: True if any ability answers to this action.
- `stop_all() -> void`: Stops every running ability, which starts their cooldowns.
- `cancel(action: StringName) -> void`: Stops whatever is running for this action, which starts its cooldown.
- `is_locked(ability: AbilityBase) -> bool`: True if this ability's category is locked out right now.
- `ticks_for(seconds: float) -> int`: Seconds as whole ticks at 60 a second, at least 1 for anything above 0.
- `needs_full_movement() -> bool`: True while an ability with needs_full_movement runs (Dash, Knockback), so the pawn moves by physics, not the CrowdMover (pawn spec 8.22).
- `get_abilities() -> AbilityBase[]`: Every ability, in run order.
- `get_knockback() -> KnockbackAbility`: This pawn's Knockback ability, or null. A KnockbackPart asks on every push.
- `is_action_running(action: StringName) -> bool`: True while any ability on this action runs. Cheap, for asking every tick: looks only at abilities with a timer going.
- `press_priority_now(ability: AbilityBase) -> int`: An ability's priority now: its own plus what effects add (AbilityPriorityPart, pawn spec 8.11), without the jitter offset.
- `interrupt_priority_now(ability: AbilityBase) -> int`: Its interrupt_priority right now, with what effects add.
- `interrupt_threshold_now(ability: AbilityBase) -> int`: Its interrupt_threshold now, with what effects add; for a stepped ability, the strictest of its running steps'.
- `open_combo_window(ticks: int) -> void`: Opens the combo window for this many ticks. An [`OpenComboStep`](#opencombostep) calls it after its ability's hit.
- `is_combo_window_open() -> bool`: True while the combo window is open.
- `combo_window_ticks_left() -> int`: Ticks left in the combo window; 0 when it's shut. For readouts.
- `combo_position_for(ability: AbilityBase) -> int`: The combo position it would take if it started now: the next, if the window is open and it fits; else 1 for an opener; else 0 (can't start now). 0 too with no combo_positions.
- `interrupt_rule(starting: AbilityBase, running: AbilityBase) -> Dictionary`: What happens if starting tries to start while running runs, by this pawn's numbers now (effects included). Ignores cooldowns and can_start.
  
  Returns {"result": "alongside" | "cancels" | "blocked", "reason": text}: alongside (no lockout between them), cancels (priority at least the threshold, or cancelled_by), blocked (a locomotion ability stops steering instead).
- `get_interrupt_table() -> Dictionary[]`: The interrupt table (pawn spec 8.10): a row per ability that can run (timed ones and locomotion), in run order, with an `interrupt_rule()` answer per other ability. Instant actions such as Jump have no row.
- `get_interrupt_table_text() -> String`: The interrupt table as text, a line per ability with what cancels it and what it blocks.
- `receive_hit(hit: HitInfo) -> void`: Something hit this pawn; the server's attacker calls it, such as a [`MeleeSweepStep`](#meleesweepstep). Dead or invulnerable pawns ignore it. During simulate it's queued and delivered after every pawn has simulated, in a fixed order (attacker's entity id, target's, queue order), so it never depends on who simulated first (pawn spec 15.4); otherwise it takes effect at once. Steps: see the README.
- `health_ran_out(hit: HitInfo) -> void`: The EffectManager calls this on the authority when an effect took Health to 0: Death starts and `died` goes out. hit is the hit that did it, or null (a poison's tick). Nothing if already dead.
- `revive() -> void`: Brings a dead pawn back with full Health, on the server. Death ends on its next tick.
- `settings_changed() -> void`: An ability's settings changed while playing (`AbilityBase.use_definition()`): its masks, priority order and lists are worked out again.

## DashAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/DashAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

A short, fast burst toward the movement input: an action bound to &"dash".

It adds acceleration along the dash direction for `speed_up_seconds`, then takes speed off for `slow_down_seconds`, so left alone the pawn ends at the speed it started with. Speed gained some other way during a dash stays. Walking, sprinting and jumping are locked out while it runs, and it works on the ground and in the air (`usable_in_air`). The pawn turns to face the dash.
It cancels a swing, and it's invulnerable for its first 0.18 s (an [`InvulnerabilityInterceptor`](#invulnerabilityinterceptor), pawn spec 8.23). Rollback: `dash_direction` rolls back with its timer and cooldown; its phase comes from `AbilityBase.ticks_before_this_run()`. Design: pawn spec 8.6, 8.9.

### Settings and properties

- `acceleration_stat: StringName`: From the definition: `DashDefinition.acceleration_stat`.
- `fallback_acceleration: float`: From the definition: `DashDefinition.fallback_acceleration`.
- `speed_up_seconds: float`: From the definition: `DashDefinition.speed_up_seconds`.
- `slow_down_deceleration: float`: From the definition: `DashDefinition.slow_down_deceleration`.
- `slow_down_seconds: float`: From the definition: `DashDefinition.slow_down_seconds`.
- `usable_in_air: bool`: From the definition: `DashDefinition.usable_in_air`.
- `dash_direction: Vector3` = `Vector3(0, 0, 0)`: The way it's dashing, flat and length 1. Rolls back (pushed).

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: With no interceptor of its own, a Dash is invulnerable for its first 0.18 s, so the end of its slow-down can be hit. Its kind's defaults: a new [`DashDefinition`](#dashdefinition).
- `make_default_interceptors() -> void`
- `get_pushed_properties() -> String[]`
- `is_timed() -> bool`: Timed, by its two phases rather than duration.
- `duration_ticks() -> int`: The speed-up's ticks plus the slow-down's.
- `can_start() -> bool`: Anywhere with usable_in_air on (the default); on the ground only with it off.
- `start() -> void`: Picks the direction (the movement input, or the facing with none) and turns the pawn to face it.
- `tick(dt: float) -> void`

## DeathAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/DeathAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

Being dead: an action with no trigger action, started when the pawn's Health reaches 0.

The EffectManager calls `AbilityManager.health_ran_out()` when an effect takes Health to 0, and the AbilityManager starts this and sends `AbilityManager.died`. While it runs it locks out movement, combat and utility, nothing cancels it, and `Pawn.is_dead()` is true (the pawn ignores its input and AI, and other pawns' sensing ignores it). It keeps running while Health is 0; `AbilityManager.revive()` ends it. The body stays where it falls: removing it or respawning is game code's job.
Rollback: its timer rolls back with Health, so clients see the pawn dead from snapshots. It watches `StatManager.HEALTH`. Design: pawn spec 8.7, 8.16.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Timed: it runs while Health is 0. Its kind's defaults: a new [`DeathDefinition`](#deathdefinition).
- `is_timed() -> bool`
- `duration_ticks() -> int`
- `start() -> void`
- `can_sleep_while_running() -> bool`
- `tick(_dt: float) -> void`

## HitInfo

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/HitInfo.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

What one hit was, handed from the attacker to the target's `AbilityManager.receive_hit()`.

Plain data, made on the server only, where hits are decided. A hit carries effects, not numbers: the attacking ability's on-hit effects say what it does, and the target's EffectManager applies them. A hit made in code gives its own, such as `Effect.make_damage(20)`. Design: pawn spec 8.6, 8.11.

### Settings and properties

- `attacker: Pawn` = `null`: Who hit.
- `target: Pawn` = `null`: Who was hit.
- `ability: AbilityBase` = `null`: The ability that hit, such as a MeleeAttackAbility.
- `tick: int` = `0`: The tick the hit happened on.
- `direction: Vector3` = `Vector3(0, 0, 0)`: Flat, length 1: from the attacker toward the target. Knockback pushes this way.
- `effects: Effect[]` = `[]`: The effects that go on the target, in order.
- `attacker_effects: Effect[]` = `[]`: The effects that go on the attacker once the hit lands (an on-hit EffectApplier that applies to itself).
- `damage_dealt: float` = `0.0`: Filled in when the hit lands: how much Health it took, after resistances. 0 before then.
- `from_interception: bool` = `false`: True for a hit an interceptor sends back after stopping one (a parry's push-back); it can't be turned away in turn (pawn spec 8.23).

### Functions

- `planned_damage() -> float`: The Health this hit's effects take before resistances, from their StatChangeParts. For readouts that show a hit before it lands.

## JumpAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/JumpAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

Jumping: an action bound to &"jump", which happens at once.

It starts from the ground, or within `coyote_time` of walking off an edge. A press a moment too early waits `buffer_window` seconds and jumps on landing; holding the key doesn't bounce, because only a press starts it. Height comes from the pawn's JumpVelocity stat, in metres per second upward. Rollback: `left_ground_at`. Design: pawn spec 8.5.

### Settings and properties

- `coyote_time: float`: From the definition: `JumpDefinition.coyote_time`.
- `left_ground_at: int` = `-4611686018427387904`: The last tick the pawn was known to be on the ground before it left it; `ON_GROUND` while it's there. Rolls back (pushed).

### Constants

- `ON_GROUND = -4611686018427387904`: `left_ground_at` while the pawn is on the ground.
- `COUNT_CAP = 100`: The most `ticks_off_ground()` counts. Anything past the coyote time counts the same.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`JumpDefinition`](#jumpdefinition).
- `get_pushed_properties() -> String[]`
- `ticks_off_ground() -> int`: Ticks since the pawn was last on the ground, up to `COUNT_CAP`; 0 on the ground.
- `every_tick(_dt: float) -> void`
- `can_sleep() -> bool`: True while on the ground: a sleeping pawn is grounded, so it would only keep it there (pawn spec 15.3).
- `can_start() -> bool`
- `start() -> void`

## KnockbackAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/KnockbackAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

Being pushed by a hit: an action with no trigger action, started by a KnockbackPart through `push()`.

It lives on the pawn being hit. For the push's duration it sets the pawn's horizontal velocity to the push, fading in a straight line to nothing, and locks out movement and combat. A push with a hop speed lifts a grounded pawn on its first tick (not one already in the air); the hop can outlast the push. A second hit while it runs starts it again with the new push. Only Dash cancels it.
Rollback: `push_velocity` and `push_ticks` roll back with its timer, so a corrected client replays the push. Design: pawn spec 8.6, 8.9.

### Settings and properties

- `push_velocity: Vector3` = `Vector3(0, 0, 0)`: The push at the start, in metres per second; its y is the hop speed upward. Rolls back (pushed).
- `push_ticks: int` = `0`: How many ticks this push lasts. Rolls back (pushed).

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`KnockbackDefinition`](#knockbackdefinition).
- `get_pushed_properties() -> String[]`
- `is_timed() -> bool`: Timed, by its push's length rather than duration.
- `duration_ticks() -> int`
- `push(velocity: Vector3, ticks: int, hop: float = 0.0) -> bool`: Starts a push; hop is the upward speed in metres per second (0: none). Returns false if something stronger is running.
- `tick(_dt: float) -> void`

## MeleeAttackAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/MeleeAttackAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

A melee swing: an action bound to &"primary", built from steps.

A swing is a [`WindupStep`](#windupstep) with a [`TurnToFaceStep`](#turntofacestep) beside it, a [`MeleeSweepStep`](#meleesweepstep) (the hit window), then an [`OpenComboStep`](#opencombostep) and a [`WaitStep`](#waitstep) for recovery. With no [`AbilityStep`](#abilitystep) children of its own it makes those from the settings below, about 0.4 s with the defaults; place steps of your own for another pattern (these settings then only matter for `attack_range`, the AI's reach, and `warns_targets`). It locks out movement and other combat; Dash cancels it, Sprint and Jump don't. Hits happen on the server only, during the sweep, and a replay never hits again. What a hit does comes from its EffectApplier children, not the swing itself. Design: pawn spec 8.6, 8.9, 8.20.

### Settings and properties

- `windup_ticks: int`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.windup_ticks`.
- `hit_ticks: int`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.hit_ticks`.
- `recovery_ticks: int`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.recovery_ticks`.
- `attack_range: float`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.attack_range`.
- `hit_radius: float`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.hit_radius`.
- `hit_height: float`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.hit_height`.
- `hits_own_team: bool`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.hits_own_team`.
- `sweep_degrees: float`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.sweep_degrees`.
- `sweep_from_left: bool`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.sweep_from_left`.
- `height_at_sweep_start: float`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.height_at_sweep_start`.
- `height_at_sweep_end: float`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.height_at_sweep_end`.
- `windup_turn_degrees_per_second: float`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.windup_turn_degrees_per_second`.
- `combo_window_ticks: int`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.combo_window_ticks`.
- `warns_targets: bool`: From the definition: `MeleeAttackDefinition.warns_targets`.

### Signals

- `hit_landed(hit: HitInfo)`: Sent on the server for each pawn the swing hits, when it finds it. The target takes the hit later in the same tick, after every pawn has simulated (pawn spec 15.4).
- `hit_window_started(centre: Vector3, radius: float)`: Sent once per sweep, on its first tick, with where the hit sphere is and its radius. Every machine that runs the swing sends it (server, offline, a predicting client), never during a replay. Says where it can hit, not whether it did: see `hit_landed`.
- `hit_area_moved(from: Vector3, to: Vector3, radius: float)`: Sent every tick of a sweep, on the same machines as `hit_window_started`, with the hit sphere's start and end for this tick.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its attack_range: the AI swings from within it. Its kind's defaults: a new [`MeleeAttackDefinition`](#meleeattackdefinition).
- `attack_reach() -> float`
- `collect_steps() -> void`: Finds its steps, after making the default ones from its settings if it has none of its own.
- `start() -> void`
- `default_timeline() -> TimelineEntry[]`: The timeline for the steps it made: Windup and TurnToFace together, Sweep when the windup is done, then OpenCombo and Recovery. With steps of its own and no timeline in its definition, they run one after another.
- `swing_phase() -> Dictionary`: Where the swing is, for visuals: "windup", "hit" or "recovery" with progress 0 to 1 (smooth between ticks), or "none".
- `hit_centre() -> Vector3`: Where the hit sphere is straight ahead: the middle of the sweep. With a sweep, see `hit_centre_at()`.
- `hit_centre_at(progress: float) -> Vector3`: Where the hit sphere is at this point of the sweep, 0 (start) to 1 (end), for the pawn's facing now. Answered by its first sweep step.
- `hit_offset_at(progress: float, facing: float) -> Vector3`: Like `hit_centre_at()`, as an offset from the pawn's feet for a facing in radians, so visuals draw the spots the hit checks. From `MeleeSweepStep.offset_at()`; straight ahead at chest height with no sweep.
- `planned_ticks() -> int`: Ticks a swing takes if its windup doesn't wait for the turn: first windup, sweep and recovery. 0 with none. For tests and tools.
- `windup_length() -> int`: Ticks the first windup lasts. It can take longer while it waits for the turn; `swing_phase()` says where it really is.
- `hit_length() -> int`: Ticks the first sweep can hit for.

## ParryAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/ParryAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

A parry stance: while it runs, a hit from the front does nothing to this pawn, and the attacker is pushed back instead.

This ability is the stance: it runs for duration (0.35 s, then a 1.5 s cooldown), turns the pawn toward where it looks and holds it still. Turning hits away is its [`ParryInterceptor`](#parryinterceptor) child's job (made by default with the 120 degree front), and what the attacker gets is that interceptor's ON_INTERCEPT EffectApplier children. Hits from the sides and back land as usual, and a knockback or a dash cancels the stance. A client sees its own stance at once; the parried hit's result arrives in snapshots. Design: pawn spec 8.15, 8.23.

### Settings and properties

- `turn_degrees_per_second: float`: From the definition: `ParryDefinition.turn_degrees_per_second`.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`ParryDefinition`](#parrydefinition).
- `tick(dt: float) -> void`
- `guard() -> ParryInterceptor`: Its [`ParryInterceptor`](#parryinterceptor), or null. The debug drawing reads the front's width from it.
- `make_default_interceptors() -> void`: With no interceptor of its own, a ParryInterceptor with the default front (120 degrees).

## RangedAttackAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/RangedAttackAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

A ranged attack: an action bound to &"primary" that fires a projectile, built from steps.

A shot is a [`WindupStep`](#windupstep) with a [`TurnToFaceStep`](#turntofacestep) beside it, a [`FireProjectileStep`](#fireprojectilestep), then a [`WaitStep`](#waitstep) for recovery. With no [`AbilityStep`](#abilitystep) children of its own it makes those from the settings below; place steps of your own for another pattern (a volley is several fire steps). It locks out movement and other combat while it runs; Dash cancels it. What a hit does comes from its EffectApplier children, carried by the projectile. Design: pawn spec 8.24.

```gdscript
# in a pawn's AbilityManager: a RangedAttack with projectile_scene set, and an EffectApplier child (on hit)
pawn.ability_manager.can_start(&"primary")
```

### Settings and properties

- `projectile_scene: PackedScene`: From the definition: `RangedAttackDefinition.projectile_scene`.
- `windup_ticks: int`: From the definition: `RangedAttackDefinition.windup_ticks`.
- `recovery_ticks: int`: From the definition: `RangedAttackDefinition.recovery_ticks`.
- `attack_range: float`: From the definition: `RangedAttackDefinition.attack_range`.
- `muzzle_height: float`: From the definition: `RangedAttackDefinition.muzzle_height`.
- `muzzle_forward: float`: From the definition: `RangedAttackDefinition.muzzle_forward`.
- `windup_turn_degrees_per_second: float`: From the definition: `RangedAttackDefinition.windup_turn_degrees_per_second`.
- `warns_targets: bool`: From the definition: `RangedAttackDefinition.warns_targets`.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its attack_range: the AI shoots from within it. Its kind's defaults: a new [`RangedAttackDefinition`](#rangedattackdefinition).
- `attack_reach() -> float`
- `collect_steps() -> void`: Finds its steps, after making the default ones from its settings if it has none of its own.
- `start() -> void`
- `default_timeline() -> TimelineEntry[]`: The timeline for the steps it made: Windup and TurnToFace together, Fire when the windup is done, then Recovery. With steps of its own and no timeline in its definition, they run one after another.

## SprintAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/SprintAbility.gd`, extends [`WalkAbility`](#walkability)

Running faster while a charge lasts: a locomotion ability bound to &"sprint".

It moves like Walk, at SprintSpeed. While &"sprint" is held and it has charge it runs instead of Walk. Sprinting drains the charge one tick per tick; `recharge_delay` after it stops, the charge refills at `recharge_rate`. It starts only with at least `min_start_charge`, so a held key on an empty charge doesn't flicker it on a tick at a time. An AI uses it by holding &"sprint".
The charge is worked out from two values set only when it starts or stops (`charge_at_switch`, `switched_at`), so nothing changes while it drains or refills (ability spec 4). `ready_at` is the tick the charge reaches the minimum, so the manager and the AI see when it can start again. Design: pawn spec 8.5.

### Settings and properties

- `max_charge: float`: From the definition: `SprintDefinition.max_charge`.
- `recharge_rate: float`: From the definition: `SprintDefinition.recharge_rate`.
- `recharge_delay: float`: From the definition: `SprintDefinition.recharge_delay`.
- `min_start_charge: float`: From the definition: `SprintDefinition.min_start_charge`.
- `charge_at_switch: int` = `0`: Ticks of charge when it last started or stopped. Rolls back (pushed).
- `switched_at: int` = `-1`: The tick it last started or stopped; -1: never, so the charge is full. Rolls back (pushed).

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Ticks of sprinting it has now: draining while it runs, refilling while it doesn't. Worked out from the tick. Its kind's defaults: a new [`SprintDefinition`](#sprintdefinition).
- `charge_ticks() -> int`
- `is_timed() -> bool`
- `get_pushed_properties() -> String[]`
- `duration_ticks() -> int`
- `start() -> void`
- `stop() -> void`
- `delay_run(ticks: int) -> void`

## WalkAbility

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/WalkAbility.gd`, extends [`AbilityBase`](#abilitybase)

Walking on the ground: accelerating, slowing, steering in the air and turning to face where it's going. The default locomotion.

Its numbers come from the pawn's stats, so a buff or a different pawn changes them: `speed_stat` (MoveSpeed), Acceleration, Deceleration, AirControl and TurnRate (degrees per second), each with a fallback for a pawn without it. The pawn adds gravity. While its category is locked out (an attack that roots the pawn) it stops steering and the pawn slows to a stop. Design: pawn spec 8.5.

### Settings and properties

- `speed_stat: StringName`: From the definition: `WalkDefinition.speed_stat`.
- `fallback_speed: float`: From the definition: `WalkDefinition.fallback_speed`.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AbilityDefinition`: Its kind's defaults: a new [`WalkDefinition`](#walkdefinition).
- `tick(dt: float) -> void`

## AbilityDefinition

`res://assets/scripts/abilities/definitions/AbilityDefinition.gd`, extends [`Resource`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_resource.html)

The settings one variant of an ability has, shared by every pawn that uses it, such as "Goblin Swing": a Resource an ability node points at (ability spec 3).

Each kind of ability has its own class with its settings added ([`MeleeAttackDefinition`](#meleeattackdefinition)); a new one starts with the kind's defaults. `based_on` makes it a variant: each setting it hasn't changed comes from its base, so changing the base changes its variants. In the inspector a variant shows its base's values, and the revert arrow on a changed one goes back to following the base.
Read-only while playing: every pawn using it shares it. A pawn that needs other numbers uses another definition (`AbilityBase.use_definition()`), or gets them from stats and effects. An ability runs with `resolved()`, the copy with every setting worked out.

### Settings and properties

- `changed_values: PackedStringArray` = `PackedStringArray()`: The settings this variant has changed from its base: set as they're edited, and saved with it. Only these are saved in a variant's file; the rest follow the base.
- `based_on: AbilityDefinition`: The definition this one is a variant of. Empty: one of its own, starting from the kind's defaults.
- `trigger_action: StringName` = `&""`: The named action that starts it, such as &"jump". Empty: only the manager starts it, as the default locomotion.
- `category: StringName` = `&""`: What it is, as a tag such as &"movement.jump". Used for lockouts. Empty: nothing can lock it out.
- `extra_categories: StringName[]` = `[]`: More groups it belongs to besides category, such as &"movement.advanced" for a dash. Lockouts, cancels and `AbilityManager.action_for_tag()` answer to all of them. They share one 64-bit mask with every other ability tag.
- `priority: int` = `0`: Which ability a press picks among those on one action: the highest that can start wins, then the first in the tree. Locomotion with a held action works the same. Effects can add to it (AbilityPriorityPart, pawn spec 8.11).
- `combo_positions: int[]` = `[]`: Which combo positions it can fill: [1] an opener, [2] a second hit, [2, 3] second or third. A follow-up (no 1) starts only while the combo window is open; give it a higher priority than the opener so it wins there. Empty: not in combos. Pawn spec 8.20.
- `priority_jitter: float` = `0.0`: A random offset, up to plus or minus this, added to priority when a press picks between abilities. 0: none. It comes from the tick's own random numbers (`TickDriver.tick_rng()`), so a replay picks the same ability. Locomotion ignores it.
- `duration: float` = `0.0`: Seconds. For an action, 0 means it happens at once. For locomotion, 0 means it runs as long as it's wanted.
- `cooldown: float` = `0.0`: Seconds after it stops before it can start again.
- `locks_out: StringName[]` = `[]`: Categories that can't start, or steer, while this runs, such as &"movement" for an attack that roots the pawn.
- `buffer_window: float` = `0.0`: Seconds a press waits if the ability can't start yet, such as jump pressed just before landing. 0: a press is tried once.
- `interrupt_priority: int` = `0`: How hard it cancels a running ability it conflicts with (pawn spec 8.6): Walk 0, Jump 5, Sprint 10, Parry 10, MeleeAttack 15, Knockback 30, Dash 40, Death 1000.
- `interrupt_threshold: int` = `100`: While it runs, a conflicting ability with at least this interrupt_priority cancels it; a weaker one is locked out. 100: only Death cancels it. MeleeAttack uses 15, so Dash cancels a swing and Sprint doesn't.
- `cancelled_by: StringName[]` = `[]`: Categories that can always cancel it while it runs, whatever the interrupt numbers say, such as &"movement.jump". A category covers its children, as in locks_out.
- `pauses_locomotion: bool` = `false`: On: locomotion (Walk, Sprint) doesn't run at all while this does, so it neither steers nor slows the pawn (Dash). Off: a locked-out locomotion still slows the pawn to a stop, as an attack that roots the pawn wants.
- `needs_full_movement: bool` = `false`: On: while it runs the pawn moves by physics (`move_and_slide`), not the CrowdMover, so fast or forced moves such as Dash and Knockback collide properly. Pawn spec 8.22.
- `step_timeline: TimelineEntry[]` = `[]`: For a stepped ability: when each step runs (ability spec 6.2), as entries in ticks from its start. Empty: its kind's default (a swing's windup, sweep and recovery), or its steps one after another.
- `max_steps_ticks: int` = `600`: For a stepped ability, the longest it can run, in ticks at 60 a second. It ends when no step runs, or at this. Ignored without steps.
- `resolved_from: AbilityDefinition` = `null`: For a resolved copy: the definition it was worked out from. Null on a definition of its own.

### Constants

- `MAX_BASE_DEPTH = 32`

### Functions

- `setting_names() -> PackedStringArray`: The names of its settings: what a variant can change.
- `value_of(setting: StringName, depth: int = 0) -> Variant`: A setting's value here: its own if it changed it or has no base, else its base's.
- `resolved() -> AbilityDefinition`: This definition with every setting worked out, the copy an ability runs with: itself when it has no base. Worked out once while playing (definitions don't change then), every time in the editor.
- `describe() -> String`: A short name for warnings and readouts: its resource_name, its file's name, or the kind.
- `is_embedded() -> bool`: True if it's saved inside a scene ("Make Unique"), not in a file of its own: a quick tweak while prototyping. Diagnostics lists them.
